passages.text: As they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent out two of His disciples and said to them, “Go into the village ahead of you, and as soon as you enter it, you will find a colt tied there, on which no one has ever sat. Untie it and bring it here.
passages.sermon:
Jesus and His disciples traveled toward Jerusalem.
They came near Bethphage and Bethany.
These villages are close to the Mount of Olives.
Jesus chose two of His disciples.
He sent them on a task.
Jesus spoke to them.
He said, “Go into the village ahead of you.
When you enter the village, you will see a colt tied there.
No one has ever sat on this colt.
Untie the colt.
Bring it here to Me.”
passages.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγγίζουσιν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα εἰς Βηθφαγὴ καὶ Βηθανίαν πρὸς τὸ ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν ἀποστέλλει δύο τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν κώμην τὴν κατέναντι ὑμῶν καὶ εὐθὺς εἰσπορευόμενοι εἰς αὐτὴν εὑρήσετε πῶλον δεδεμένον ἐφ’ ὃν οὐδεὶς οὔπω ἀνθρώπων ἐκάθισεν λύσατε αὐτὸν καὶ φέρετε

passages.text: If anyone asks, ‘Why are you doing this?’ tell him, ‘The Lord needs it and will return it shortly.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to two of His disciples.
He gave them instructions.
He said, “If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ answer them this way.
Say, ‘The Lord needs the colt.
He will send it back here soon.’”
passages.original: καὶ ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ Τί ποιεῖτε τοῦτο εἴπατε Ὅτι Ὁ Κύριος αὐτοῦ χρείαν ἔχει καὶ εὐθὺς αὐτὸν ἀποστέλλει πάλιν ὧδε

passages.text: So they went and found the colt outside in the street, tied at a doorway. They untied it, and some who were standing there asked, “Why are you untying the colt?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus sent two of His disciples.
The two disciples went to the village.
They found a colt tied outside at a doorway in the street.
They untied the colt.
Some people were standing there.
These people asked the disciples, “Why are you untying the colt?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπῆλθον καὶ εὗρον πῶλον δεδεμένον πρὸς θύραν ἔξω ἐπὶ τοῦ ἀμφόδου καὶ λύουσιν αὐτόν καί τινες τῶν ἐκεῖ ἑστηκότων ἔλεγον αὐτοῖς Τί ποιεῖτε λύοντες τὸν πῶλον

passages.text: The disciples answered as Jesus had instructed them, and the people gave them permission.
passages.sermon: Jesus gave instructions to His disciples.\r\nThe disciples spoke to the people as Jesus had told them.\r\nThe people allowed the disciples to take the colt.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτοῖς καθὼς εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἀφῆκαν αὐτούς

passages.text: Then they led the colt to Jesus and threw their cloaks over it, and He sat on it.
passages.sermon: The disciples brought the colt to Jesus.\r\nThey placed their cloaks on the colt.\r\nJesus sat on the colt.
passages.original: καὶ φέρουσιν τὸν πῶλον πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ ἐπιβάλλουσιν αὐτῷ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐπ’ αὐτόν

passages.text: Many in the crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others spread branches they had cut from the fields.
passages.sermon:
Many people stood in the crowd.
Some people took off their cloaks.
They spread their cloaks on the road.
Other people cut branches from the fields.
They spread the branches on the road.
passages.original: Καὶ πολλοὶ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν ἔστρωσαν εἰς τὴν ὁδόν ἄλλοι δὲ στιβάδας κόψαντες ἐκ τῶν ἀγρῶν

passages.text: The ones who went ahead and those who followed were shouting: “Hosanna!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus entered Jerusalem riding on a colt.
Many people walked in front of Jesus.
Many people followed behind Jesus.
The people shouted loudly.
They said, “Hosanna!”
They said, “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!”
passages.original: καὶ οἱ προάγοντες καὶ οἱ ἀκολουθοῦντες ἔκραζον Ὡσαννά Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου

passages.text: “Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!” “Hosanna in the highest!”
passages.sermon:
The crowd spoke about the kingdom of God.
They called this kingdom the coming kingdom.
They said this kingdom belonged to their father David.
They said, “Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!”
They also shouted, “Hosanna in the highest!”
passages.original: Εὐλογημένη ἡ ἐρχομένη βασιλεία τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Δαυίδ Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις

passages.text: Then Jesus entered Jerusalem and went into the temple courts. He looked around at everything, but since it was already late, He went out to Bethany with the Twelve.
passages.sermon:
Jesus entered Jerusalem.
He went into the temple courts.
He looked around at everything in the temple.
It was already late.
Jesus left the temple.
He went out to Bethany.
The Twelve disciples went with Him.
passages.original: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα εἰς τὸ ἱερόν καὶ περιβλεψάμενος πάντα ὀψὲ ἤδη οὔσης τῆς ὥρας ἐξῆλθεν εἰς Βηθανίαν μετὰ τῶν δώδεκα

passages.text: The next day, when they had left Bethany, Jesus was hungry.
passages.sermon: Jesus left Bethany with His disciples the next day.\r\nJesus felt hungry.
passages.original: Καὶ τῇ ἐπαύριον ἐξελθόντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Βηθανίας ἐπείνασεν

passages.text: Seeing in the distance a fig tree in leaf, He went to see if there was any fruit on it. But when He reached it, He found nothing on it except leaves, since it was not the season for figs.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw a fig tree far away.
The fig tree had leaves.
Jesus went to the fig tree.
He wanted to see if there was any fruit on it.
He reached the fig tree.
He found only leaves on the tree.
He did not find any fruit.
It was not the season for figs.
passages.original: καὶ ἰδὼν συκῆν ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔχουσαν φύλλα ἦλθεν εἰ ἄρα τι εὑρήσει ἐν αὐτῇ καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐπ’ αὐτὴν οὐδὲν εὗρεν εἰ μὴ φύλλα ὁ γὰρ καιρὸς οὐκ ἦν σύκων

passages.text: Then He said to the tree, “May no one ever eat of your fruit again.” And His disciples heard this statement.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the fig tree.\r\nHe said, “May no one ever eat fruit from you again.”\r\nHis disciples heard what Jesus said.
passages.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτῇ Μηκέτι εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἐκ σοῦ μηδεὶς καρπὸν φάγοι καὶ ἤκουον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: When they arrived in Jerusalem, Jesus entered the temple courts and began to drive out those who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.
passages.sermon:
Jesus and His disciples arrived in Jerusalem.
Jesus entered the temple courts.
Jesus saw people buying and selling in the temple.
Jesus began to drive out those who were selling in the temple.
Jesus also drove out those who were buying in the temple.
Jesus overturned the tables of the money changers.
Jesus overturned the seats of those who sold doves.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα Καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἤρξατο ἐκβάλλειν τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ τοὺς ἀγοράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ τὰς τραπέζας τῶν κολλυβιστῶν καὶ τὰς καθέδρας τῶν πωλούντων τὰς περιστερὰς κατέστρεψεν

passages.text: And He would not allow anyone to carry merchandise through the temple courts.
passages.sermon:
Jesus entered the temple courts in Jerusalem.
He saw people buying and selling there.
He acted with authority.
He did not allow anyone to carry merchandise through the temple courts.
passages.original: καὶ οὐκ ἤφιεν ἵνα τις διενέγκῃ σκεῦος διὰ τοῦ ἱεροῦ

passages.text: Then Jesus began to teach them, and He declared, “Is it not written: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations’? But you have made it ‘a den of robbers.’”
passages.sermon:
Jesus began to teach the people in the temple.
He spoke to them directly.
He said, “God has written these words.
‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations.’
But you have made it a den of robbers.”
passages.original: καὶ ἐδίδασκεν καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Οὐ γέγραπται ὅτι Ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς κληθήσεται πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ὑμεῖς δὲ πεποιήκατε αὐτὸν Σπήλαιον λῃστῶν

passages.text: When the chief priests and scribes heard this, they looked for a way to kill Him. For they were afraid of Him, because the whole crowd was astonished at His teaching.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests heard Jesus.
The scribes also heard Jesus.
They wanted to kill Jesus.
They looked for a way to do this.
They were afraid of Jesus.
The whole crowd was amazed at Jesus’ teaching.
This made the chief priests and scribes afraid.
passages.original: Καὶ ἤκουσαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ ἐζήτουν πῶς αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν ἐφοβοῦντο γὰρ αὐτόν πᾶς γὰρ ὁ ὄχλος ἐξεπλήσσετο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And when evening came, Jesus and His disciples went out of the city.
passages.sermon: Jesus was with His disciples.\r\nEvening came.\r\nJesus and His disciples left the city.
passages.original: Καὶ ὅταν ὀψὲ ἐγένετο ἐξεπορεύοντο ἔξω τῆς πόλεως

passages.text: As they were walking back in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from its roots.
passages.sermon:
Jesus and His disciples walked in the morning.
They passed by the place where the fig tree stood.
They saw the fig tree.
The fig tree had withered.
It was withered from its roots.
passages.original: Καὶ παραπορευόμενοι πρωῒ εἶδον τὴν συκῆν ἐξηραμμένην ἐκ ῥιζῶν

passages.text: Peter remembered it and said, “Look, Rabbi! The fig tree You cursed has withered.”
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter saw the fig tree.
Peter remembered what happened before.
Peter spoke to Jesus.
Peter said, “Rabbi, look!”
Peter said, “The fig tree you cursed has withered.”
passages.original: καὶ ἀναμνησθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος λέγει αὐτῷ Ῥαββί ἴδε ἡ συκῆ ἣν κατηράσω ἐξήρανται

passages.text: “Have faith in God,” Jesus said to them.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to them.\r\nJesus said, "Have faith in God."
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς Ἔχετε πίστιν θεοῦ

passages.text: “Truly I tell you that if anyone says to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ and has no doubt in his heart but believes that it will happen, it will be done for him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, "Truly, I tell you this."
If any person speaks to this mountain,
and says, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,'
and does not doubt in his heart,
but believes that what he says will happen,
then it will be done for him."
passages.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ὃς ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ Ἄρθητι καὶ βλήθητι εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ μὴ διακριθῇ ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ πιστεύῃ ὅτι ὃ λαλεῖ γίνεται ἔσται αὐτῷ

passages.text: Therefore I tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus told them to have faith in God.
He said, “When you pray, ask God for what you need.
Believe that you have already received what you ask for.
If you believe, you will receive it.”
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν πάντα ὅσα προσεύχεσθε καὶ αἰτεῖσθε πιστεύετε ὅτι ἐλάβετε καὶ ἔσται ὑμῖν

passages.text: And when you stand to pray, if you hold anything against another, forgive it, so that your Father in heaven will forgive your trespasses as well.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus taught about prayer.
When you stand and pray, forgive others.
If you have anything against anyone, let it go.
Forgive that person.
Then your Father in heaven will forgive your sins.
passages.original: Καὶ ὅταν στήκετε προσευχόμενοι ἀφίετε εἴ τι ἔχετε κατά τινος ἵνα καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς ἀφῇ ὑμῖν τὰ παραπτώματα ὑμῶν

passages.text: After their return to Jerusalem, Jesus was walking in the temple courts, and the chief priests, scribes, and elders came up to Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus and His followers returned to Jerusalem.
Jesus walked in the temple courts.
The chief priests saw Jesus.
The scribes saw Jesus.
The elders saw Jesus.
The chief priests, scribes, and elders approached Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται πάλιν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ περιπατοῦντος αὐτοῦ ἔρχονται πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι

passages.text: “By what authority are You doing these things?” they asked. “And who gave You the authority to do them?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in the temple courts in Jerusalem.
The chief priests, scribes, and elders came to Jesus.
They spoke to Jesus.
They asked Jesus a question.
They said, “By what authority are you doing these things?”
They also asked, “Who gave you the authority to do them?”
passages.original: καὶ ἔλεγον αὐτῷ Ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς ἢ τίς σοι ἔδωκεν τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην ἵνα ταῦτα ποιῇς

passages.text: “I will ask you one question,” Jesus replied, “and if you answer Me, I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in the temple courts in Jerusalem.
The chief priests, scribes, and elders came to Him.
Jesus spoke to them.
He said, “I will ask you one question.
If you answer Me, I will tell you by what authority I do these things.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἐπερωτήσω ὑμᾶς ἕνα λόγον καὶ ἀποκρίθητέ μοι καὶ ἐρῶ ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ

passages.text: John’s baptism—was it from heaven or from men? Answer Me!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the religious leaders.
He asked them a question.
He said, “John baptized people.
Did John’s baptism come from heaven?
Or did John’s baptism come from men?
Answer Me.”
passages.original: τὸ βάπτισμα τὸ Ἰωάννου ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἦν ἢ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἀποκρίθητέ μοι

passages.text: They deliberated among themselves what they should answer: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’
passages.sermon:
The religious leaders talked to each other.
They tried to decide what answer to give Jesus.
They said, “What should we say?”
They considered one option.
They said, “If we say, ‘John’s baptism was from heaven,’ Jesus will ask us a question.”
He will ask, ‘Why did you not believe John?’
passages.original: Καὶ διελογίζοντο πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς λέγοντες Τί εἴπωμεν Ἐὰν εἴπωμεν Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐρεῖ Διὰ τί οὖν οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ

passages.text: But if we say, ‘From men’...” they were afraid of the people, for they all held that John truly was a prophet.
passages.sermon:
The religious leaders considered their answer.
They thought about saying, “John’s baptism was from men.”
They felt afraid of the crowd.
All the people believed John was truly a prophet.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ εἴπωμεν Ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἐφοβοῦντο τὸν ὄχλον ἅπαντες γὰρ εἶχον τὸν Ἰωάννην ὄντως ὅτι προφήτης ἦν

passages.text: So they answered, “We do not know.” And Jesus replied, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.”
passages.sermon:
The religious leaders spoke to Jesus.
They answered Him.
They said, “We do not know.”
Jesus replied to them.
He said, “I will not tell you by what authority I do these things.”
passages.original: καὶ ἀποκριθέντες τῷ Ἰησοῦ λέγουσιν Οὐκ οἴδαμεν Καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς Οὐδὲ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ
